fact: The Ram's brightest star — once the marker of the spring equinox.
bio: Hamal (Alpha Arietis) is an orange giant about 66 light-years away, the brightest star in Aries the Ram, and it hosts a giant planet detected from its motion.
cultural: The name is Arabic for 'the lamb' or 'ram'. Around two thousand years ago the Sun crossed the vernal equinox near Hamal, so the 'First Point of Aries' — still the zero of celestial longitude — carries the Ram's name even though precession has since moved the crossing into Pisces.
